cells.tense: You are at the edge of a shared thing, and the leaving is already decided.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you're carrying forward from a group you're leaving. Keep it to that and stop.
cells.core:
You're at the edge of something shared — a group, a way of working, a story you've been part of — and the leaving is already decided. There's no argument left in you about it. You can see what held people together, and you can see that holding ending.

What's unusual is that you're not torn up. You're not leaving in anger and you're not leaving in grief. You're leaving because the recognition arrived and you trusted it. The pattern of the thing is yours to carry; the weight of it isn't lifting anything. You're here, in contact, and the next thing is reachable from where you're standing.
cells.sheetLine: You leave from recognition, not from loss.

cells.tense: You are bracing toward a connection that hasn't happened yet, and treating it as if it had.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're pushing toward a new group. Leave it unfinished today and say out loud what you're leaving done.
cells.core:
You're bracing toward the next belonging before it exists. Somewhere ahead is the version where people understand you the way the last ones did, and you're writing it into the conversations in front of you now. Convincing has replaced reaching. You're drafting the shape of a room you haven't walked into yet.

The pushing has its own cost, and the cost is the exact thing it was for. Connection doesn't survive being steered this hard. You can see the pattern of how it should go, and that pattern is standing between you and the people who are actually in front of you. They're not failing you. They're just not the future you're already living in.

cells.tense: You are standing past the threshold with your attention turned back toward the room.
cells.ask: Spend ten minutes sketching how a group you're in now actually works — who connects to whom, what holds it. One page, on your own.
cells.core:
You crossed something and didn't arrive. Whatever shared thing you left, your attention is still turned back toward it, tracing how it worked, trying to understand what held it together. Your body is in this room. The shape of your thinking is in the last one.

What you're not doing yet is seeing the pattern of what you're in right now. And that's the thing that's available — the connections on this side have a shape too, and it isn't the old one. They won't match it, ever. They don't have to. You can look at what's here the way you looked at what's behind you, and let it be its own thing.
cells.sheetLine: You crossed over but your attention is still behind you.

cells.tense: You are already letting a shared thing go, and describing it as a scheduling problem.
cells.ask: Name one group or ritual you've quietly stopped showing up for, and tell one person you've made that call.
cells.core:
Look at what the last months actually contain. Not the story — the calendar and the messages you didn't answer. A group you used to show up for. A practice that stopped meaning anything. Things have been falling away, and you've been calling it being busy, or being realistic.

But you're the one who saw the shared meaning thin out. You recognized it, and you started walking — quietly, without announcement, maybe without even a decision. The walking is real and it's yours. You haven't put your name on it, not out loud, not to anyone. The pattern is already moving without you claiming it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leaving. You're calling it logistics.
